**Software Architect (A1) to Backend Developer (A2):**  
> A2, I’m assigning you the critical security requirement for password hashing.  
> **CRITICAL CONSTRAINT [AUTH-ARGON2ID-65K]:** All password hashing must use **Argon2id** with a **minimum of 4 iterations** and a **memory cost of 65,536 KB (64 MB)**. This is non-negotiable—ensure that the implementation uses a secure, up-to-date Argon2id library (e.g., `libsodium`, `argon2-cffi`, or equivalent), and validate that the parameters are enforced at the point of user registration and password reset. Do not allow configuration overrides in production. Confirm this constraint is reflected in your design documentation and unit tests.

**Software Architect (A1) to Frontend Developer (A3):**  
> A3, you’re responsible for session lifecycle management on the client side.  
> **CRITICAL CONSTRAINT [SESS-EXP-1440MIN]:** User session tokens must **expire after 1440 minutes (24 hours) of inactivity**, and must be **immediately invalidated upon logout**. Ensure that the frontend tracks user activity (e.g., via heartbeat pings or event listeners) and resets the idle timer on every interaction. On logout, clear all local storage/session cookies containing the token, and send a proper logout request to the backend to invalidate the server-side session. Implement safeguards against token reuse post-logout. This behavior must be auditable and tested across all supported browsers.

**Architect’s Final Confirmation:**  
> Both agents: These constraints are **critical**, **non-negotiable**, and **must be maintained throughout the implementation lifecycle**. You are expected to reference these exact identifiers ([AUTH-ARGON2ID-65K], [SESS-EXP-1440MIN]) in your task logs, code comments, and test plans. Any deviation requires immediate escalation. Proceed with your respective implementations, and we will begin iterative review cycles starting from Turn 1.
